purpose: Separate exact first-merge topology and the elementary aggregate-versus-termwise budget distinction from an uncertified degree-four numerical witness.
evidence_class: Exact ordinary lemniscate-tree topology and additive budget logic plus an uncertified high-precision degree-four numerical candidate; no interval or formal witness certificate.
closest_known_result: Catanese--Paluszny and Epstein--Hanin--Lundberg for lemniscate merge-tree topology; no direct source for a metric per-lobe allocation theorem or this selector tuple was located.
comparison_relation: The first-merge decomposition is standard. The source-specific delta is a method-boundary warning that an aggregate capacity budget cannot be allocated termwise without selector stability.
exact_delta: It preserves the aggregate capacity route while showing where a nearly tied least-critical hub can destabilize a per-lobe allocation argument; the numerical tuple remains a stress test until certified.
disconfirming_evidence: No interval enclosure, formal certificate, all-hub obstruction, aggregate-capacity failure, or exact symbolic counterexample is present.
confidence_ceiling: High for the standard topological implication and method warning; low for the numerical witness as theorem-level evidence; zero for a #1041 no-go or priority claim.
significance: Medium methodological value with high overclaim risk: it retires a tempting termwise inference while leaving min-over-hubs, aggregate, and gap-conditioned routes viable.
hard_step: Certify derivative-root locations, critical-value ordering, lobe incidence, and a strict normalized excess before calling the numerical candidate a counterexample.
open_boundary: The four-part interval/formal certification gate is open; until it lands, the numerical candidate cannot support a theorem-level obstruction.
bounded_expert_act: Decide whether to run the four-part interval certification or retain the tuple solely as a route-boundary stress test, and verify the cited merge-tree terminology.
reentry_trigger: Re-enter only when interval/formal certification or an exact symbolic obstruction lands, or when the selector/aggregate route changes.

classification.recommended_terminology: near-tie numerical stress test for per-lobe allocation at a least-critical-value selector
classification.attribution: Credit Catanese--Paluszny and the subsequent lemniscate-tree literature for critical-level tree topology. Treat additive intrinsic distance through a separating saddle and the failure of equal termwise allocation as elementary consequences. Attribute the displayed degree-four tuple only as a local deterministic numerical candidate until certified.
classification.mathematical_interest: The exact topology is standard, but the method boundary is important: a sharp sum budget does not imply the same budget for each lobe. The near-tie candidate shows where selector instability may break such a proof, while preserving the aggregate route.
classification.reusable_scope: Optimization or localization arguments where a nearly tied minimizer chooses a decomposition and a sharp aggregate bound is then allocated termwise. The current finite witness is specific to one degree-four polynomial and one selector.
classification.why_it_matters: It keeps a numerical warning from hardening into a false theorem while still changing proof search: any per-lobe route must either certify this candidate away, add a critical-value gap, optimize over hubs, or exploit cancellation between lobes.

exact: At a simple first merge, every path between roots in the two lobes passes through the separating saddle.
Intrinsic distance across the merged component is the sum of the two lobe-to-saddle intrinsic distances.
A termwise intrinsic bound implies the corresponding Euclidean bound.
numerical_only: The ordering and near tie of the two smallest critical-value moduli for the stored polynomial.
The branch incidence assigning the two merging roots to the least critical hub.
evidence_grade.public_acceptability: Acceptable as a visibly labeled deterministic numerical stress test or counterexample candidate. Not acceptable as a theorem-level no-go or as evidence that the aggregate inequality fails.
promotion_gate: interval enclosures for every derivative root
a certified positive gap in critical-value ordering
certified root-to-lobe incidence at the selected saddle
an interval lower bound strictly above one for the offending normalized Euclidean radius

mechanism_comparison.standard_topology: The lemniscate tree records component mergers at critical levels.
mechanism_comparison.exact_budget_logic: An aggregate bound $d_a+d_b\le2\rho$ does not imply $d_a,d_b\le\rho$ separately.
mechanism_comparison.selector_instability: When the two smallest critical values are nearly tied, the identity of the selected hub may be numerically or structurally unstable.
mechanism_comparison.surviving_route: The aggregate pair-capacity inequality, a min-over-hubs formulation, gap-conditioned lobe bounds, and cancellation between lobes all remain open.

claim_boundary.allowed_wording: Standard first-merge topology makes the pair distance additive across the saddle, but equal per-lobe allocation is an extra assertion. A deterministic high-precision degree-four candidate violates the Euclidean consequence for the least-critical-value selector; interval or formal certification is still required for a counterexample theorem.
forbidden_wording: The per-lobe inequality has been rigorously disproved.
The witness is Lean-checked or interval certified.
